title: How touchscreens work
examples: Does every touchscreen use the same technology?
What is the difference between resistive and capacitive screens?
Can I use a regular pen on a touchscreen?

explain.say: Today we learn how touchscreens actually work.
First we need to know about capacitive screens.
These screens detect changes in electricity when you touch them.
Your body naturally carries a small electric charge.
The screen has a hidden grid of sensors underneath the glass.
When you touch, your charge interacts with the sensor grid.

faq.q: Do all touchscreens work the same way?
faq.a: No, some older screens use different methods to detect touch. Resistive screens use pressure, while capacitive screens use electrical charge.
asks: What is the difference between screen types?
Do I need to press hard to use it?

faq.q: What is capacitance in this context?
faq.a: Capacitance is the ability to store an electric charge. Your finger changes the screen's capacitance when it touches it.
asks: What does 'capacitive' mean for a screen?

faq.q: Can I use a stylus or a glove?
faq.a: Many modern screens are designed to work with styluses that mimic your finger's charge. Some specialized gloves can also work.

faq.q: What is the sensor grid doing?
faq.a: The sensor grid is a network of tiny electrical points embedded below the surface. It measures where the electrical change occurs.
asks: What is the purpose of the grid?

faq.q: Does the screen need to be wet to work?
faq.a: No, while water can sometimes affect electrical readings, modern screens are designed to work reliably with dry fingers.
asks: Can I touch it if my hands are damp?

facts: Capacitive screens detect changes in an electrical field.
Your body provides the necessary electrical charge for detection.
A grid of sensors reads the location of this charge change.
These screens work best with materials that conduct electricity.

quiz.say: If a screen detects a change in its electrical field, what technology is it most likely using?
quiz.why: Capacitive screens are specifically designed to detect changes in electrical fields caused by touch.

wrong.0: Magnetic detection requires metal objects, which is not the primary method here.
wrong.1: Optical screens usually measure light changes, not electrical ones.
wrong.3: Resistive screens detect physical pressure, not electrical changes.

quiz.say: What part of the touchscreen is responsible for mapping the touch point?
quiz.why: The grid acts like a map, pinpointing exactly where the electrical change happened.

wrong.0: Pixels show the image; the grid detects the touch location.
wrong.2: The glass layer is the visible part, but the grid underneath does the sensing.
wrong.3: Your finger charge is the input, not the mapping tool itself.

quiz.say: A stylus works on a capacitive screen because:
quiz.why: For the screen to read the touch, the input must carry enough electrical charge, which the stylus does.

wrong.0: While true, 'mimicking the body's charge' is the specific functional requirement.
wrong.2: Material composition is not the main factor; the charge is.
wrong.3: If it only applied pressure, the screen would read it as a resistive touch.
